plan: [ This is a sealed-bid second-price (Vickrey) auction with three bidders. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value to maximize expected profit, independent of others’ strategies or history. Bidding below my value risks losing profitable wins; bidding above risks negative profit if I win and pay above my value. With 0.1 bid increments and no useful history in a single round, I will bid exactly my value. ]

[ In a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. This maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. With value $6 and no informative history (single round), bid 6. If competitors’ top bid is below 6, we win and pay that bid, yielding positive surplus; if above 6, we lose with zero payoff. Overbidding risks negative payoff; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, bid truthfully at 6.0. ]

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction with private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. With value 0, any positive bid risks winning and paying a positive second price, yielding negative profit. Bidding 0 ensures never overpaying; if others also bid 0, winning yields zero profit, which is acceptable. With no history and only one round, there’s no strategic signaling value. Therefore, bid exactly 0 to maximize expected profit (avoid losses). ]
